sights.address: Near JR Ōtori Station, Sakai, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Ichinomiya (first shrine) of old Izumi Province, c. 1,900 years old, enshrining Yamato Takeru; a five-minute walk from JR Ōtori Station.
Ancient Kōyasan Shingon temple (founded 701, restored by Kūkai 815) holding the National Treasure Nyoirin Kannon and Kondō hall; plum, cherry and autumn-leaf spot.
Mountain temple patronised by Toyotomi Hideyoshi (his letter survives here), with National Treasure Buddhist statues shown in autumn special exhibitions.

sights.n: Chikatsu Asuka Museum (大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館)
sights.w: Tadao Ando's stepped kofun-shaped museum of Japan's burial-mound age, set in the Chikatsu Asuka Fudoki-no-Oka tomb park.
Sakai Zen temple founded by Miyoshi Nagayoshi, burned in the 1615 Siege of Osaka and rebuilt by the monk Takuan in 1617; tea-ceremony links to Sen no Rikyū.
Temple founded 744 whose 1834 three-storey pagoda is the only one standing in Osaka Prefecture; reached on the retro Showa-era Mizuma Railway.

sights.address: In front of Hamadera Ekimae / Hamadera-kōen Station, Sakai & Takaishi, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: One of the prefecture's oldest parks (1873), a seaside pine grove at the end of the Hankai tram; the Tatsuno Kingo-office Hamadera-kōen station building is a rare Meiji survivor.
Museum of the Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri — the September festival where carved wooden floats are hauled at a run round street corners.
Hundertwasser-designed waste plant on an artificial island — red, black and white walls, a golden onion tower and roof greenery; free guided interior tours by reservation.

sights.address: Tempozan Park, Chikkō, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: 'Japan's lowest mountain' — a 4.5 m summit marker inside a harbourside park with a hidden cherry-blossom grove and an Emperor Meiji monument; 7 min from Osakakō Station.

sights.address: Tempozan Harbor Village, 1 Kaigan-dōri, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: The harbour mall at the heart of Tempozan Harbor Village, beside the Ferris wheel and Kaiyūkan; inside are the retro Shōwa food alley Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokochō and LEGOLAND Discovery Center Osaka.
Kawachi's ichinomiya at the foot of the Ikoma range, said to date back 2,600+ years; famous for its plum grove and the 23 December 'laughing ritual' (Owarai Shinji).

sights.n: Ishikiri Tsurugiya Shrine (石切劔箭神社)
sights.w: 'Ishikiri-san', the god of swellings — nationally known for the ohyakudo-mairi, worshippers circling between the stones and the hall, and a fortune-teller-lined approach street.
Japan's largest greenhouse botanical garden, built as Osaka's pavilion for Expo '90 in Tsurumi Ryokuchi Park — ~15,000 plants of 5,500 species.
Birthplace of Japanese malt whisky (built 1923): whisky museum, paid tastings and a lottery-entry production tour; 10 min walk from JR Yamazaki / Hankyu Ōyamazaki.

sights.n: Open-Air Museum of Old Japanese Farmhouses (日本民家集落博物館)
sights.w: Japan's first open-air museum (1956), in Hattori Ryokuchi Park: 11 relocated 17th-19th-century folk houses from Iwate to Amami Ōshima.
En no Gyōja-founded temple on the Minoo Falls trail, home to one of Japan's four great Benzaiten and billed as the birthplace of the Japanese lottery; 15 min walk from Hankyu Minoh.
Shrine to Ame-no-Iwafune, a 12 m boat-shaped boulder up the Amanogawa valley; the 'iwa-kuguri' rock-cave crawl beneath the giant stones is open to visitors.

sights.n: Hirakatashuku Kagiya Museum (枚方宿鍵屋資料館)
sights.w: Edo-period riverside inn where travellers waited for the Fushimi-Osaka riverboats on the Kyō-kaidō post town; a cultural property, opened as a museum in 2001.

sights.n: Engyō-ji (Mount Shosha, 書写山圓教寺)
sights.w: Atmospheric 1,000-year-old mountain temple complex 30 min from Himeji by bus and ropeway; the Mitsunodō halls were a set for The Last Samurai.
Kōyasan's central temple complex, founded where Kūkai found his thrown sankosho in a pine; dominated by the Kondō hall and the vermilion Konpon Daitō pagoda.
